developments.title: Prompt preview UI added to steeldotdev agent tool
detail: Niko (steeldotdev) added a prompt preview feature to their project, allowing users to view the exact text that will be sent to an AI agent before execution.
The preview is generated programmatically for each case, ensuring it reflects the specific context and tailored prompt.
This change aims to reduce blind trust in large, generated prompts by giving users visibility into the agent's instructions.
developments.why_it_matters: Seeing the full prompt before sending it lets users verify and edit the instructions, improving safety and control when interacting with AI agents.

developments.title: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers major reported efficiency gains over competing models
detail: Multiple commentators report that GPT-6.1 Sol achieves efficiency improvements over prior and competing models, with figures of roughly three times the efficiency of Opus 5.5, 2.5 times that of Sonnet 5.5, and 14.5 times the efficiency of GPT-5.6 at comparable intelligence.
A quoted benchmark shows GPT-6.1 Sol reaching a performance score of 44 for $6.56 compared with GPT-5.6 Sol's 43.5 for $95.35.
These claims remain reported rather than independently verified.
developments.why_it_matters: If confirmed, the efficiency gain would let developers obtain comparable AI capabilities at a fraction of prior compute cost, with substantial implications for the pricing of high-performance AI services.

developments.title: AVB releases bev-decider-0.4B, an open-weight decision model invariant to choice order
detail: AVB released bev-decider-0.4B, a lightweight causal decision model whose architecture is invariant to the order of the input choices. The model is built on the first 20 layers of Qwen and processes the prompt and choices together in one parallel forward pass, reportedly running at roughly 50 ms even on a three-year-old Mac without speed optimizations. The dataset, code, and weights are all open source, the package is pip installable, and it exposes a Jev-compatible /v1/systemone API, with benchmark details posted on the Hugging Face model page.

In the accompanying post, AVB said a 1+ hour "Jev from scratch" video is being filmed covering how to build decision datasets, network architectures for choice-order invariance, implementation with PyTorch and HF Transformers, and the full training loop and evals, with the complete project video set to drop this week.
developments.why_it_matters: Anyone can now pip install a sub-100 ms decision model whose outputs do not depend on choice ordering, inspect its open weights, dataset, and code, or plug it into Jev-compatible setups via the /v1/systemone API as of today.

developments.title: Palisade Research releases first batch of interviews with 22 current and former OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic employees
detail: Palisade Research published the first batch of interviews it conducted with 22 current and former employees from OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic. The sessions center on each participant's personal views and fears about AI development.
The organization made the first batch available on the day of the announcement and is asking viewers to watch and share the material.
developments.why_it_matters: Direct first-hand accounts from 22 people inside OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic are now publicly available, giving outside audiences immediate access to how these lab employees describe their own concerns about AI development.

developments.title: Claude Cloud Sessions receive $250 free credits
detail: Claude Cloud Sessions now offer $250 in free credits for eligible users. Users can claim the credits by typing the '/claim-credit' command in Claude Code.
The credits enable running full threads in the cloud, allowing developers to work without keeping a laptop open during a session.
developments.why_it_matters: The free credits give developers immediate, cost‑free access to cloud‑hosted Claude resources, lowering the barrier to experiment with AI agents.

developments.title: Nick Khami introduces callbay, an AI phone agent that runs inside Claude Code and Codex
detail: Nick Khami announced callbay, an AI agent that places and handles phone calls on behalf of users for tasks such as canceling subscriptions, booking medical appointments and dinners, and changing flights.
The agent is designed to run inside Claude Code and Codex, letting terminal-based workflows trigger phone tasks without switching to a separate messaging or calling app.
Khami said he has used it for dozens of phone tasks and positioned callbay as a developer-facing tool, with the call4.me site offering prepaid credits starting at $10 and a one-prompt install.
developments.why_it_matters: Callbay moves AI agent functionality into the terminal alongside Claude Code and Codex, giving developers a way to offload phone-based chores without breaking their command-line workflow or juggling a separate calling app.

developments.title: Titus agent's screenless mode streams and reads live notes from the OpenAI DevDay 2026 keynote
detail: The Titus agent was showcased with a new screenless mode that streams live-generated notes and reads them aloud, demonstrated while following the OpenAI DevDay 2026 keynote.

For the keynote, the mode streams the presentation in a small player while displaying the notes; tapping any passage jumps the video to that moment, and a Reading mode reads the notes aloud with a generated voice.

The broader screenless setup keeps a phone unplugged all day, relying on a voice-driven AI assistant that aggregates responses from Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Grok Build, Cursor, Devin, Meta's Muse and other models running on a Mac and in the cloud.
developments.why_it_matters: Hands-free, voice-driven access to live events and multiple AI models lets users follow long streams and stay productive without watching a screen, reducing screen fatigue while improving accessibility and multitasking.

developments.title: Context Language Models (CLMs) announced for self‑managed context handling
detail: Rulin Shao introduced Context Language Models (CLMs) that can natively manage their own context and treat context as a file.
CLMs learn context-management policies directly in model weights, removing the need for external harnesses.
The approach aims to let large language models control context without human‑designed pipelines.
developments.why_it_matters: By embedding context management in the model, CLMs could simplify AI toolchains and reduce reliance on custom engineering for prompt handling.

developments.title: Factory terminates Chris Degnan as board observer and advisor over contacts with Cognition
detail: Factory's chief executive, Matan Grinberg, announced the immediate termination of Chris Degnan's roles as Board Observer and Advisor to Factory after more than a year of service. According to Grinberg, Degnan first described a conversation with a Cognition executive as casual and one-off, then disclosed that evening that it was in fact formal and recurring — weeks of contact while Degnan advised Factory's leadership on confidential board-level matters under confidentiality obligations. Grinberg wrote that Factory does not know the extent of the information shared, and that Degnan's timely questions about Factory's product roadmap and product-parity gap now read differently in that light.

In the same announcement, Grinberg alleged that Cognition, the larger competitor behind the Devin coding agent, has sent engineers to fake interviews at Factory to extract product information and has offered money to people with direct knowledge of Factory's confidential plans; he also cited Factory's momentum, saying its team has grown tenfold and revenue has grown a hundredfold year over year. These claims are presented solely from Factory's side, and no response from Cognition or Degnan is included.
developments.why_it_matters: Factory has severed a year-long board-level relationship with an advisor who sat in its board meetings and heard confidential plans, while stating it cannot determine how much of that information reached Cognition, its largest competitor in coding agents. This puts Factory's confidential roadmap and product details at the center of an active dispute between two AI coding-agent makers.

developments.title: DSPyOSS hosts live walkthrough of Jev/System One implementation and ReAnchor optimizer
detail: DSPyOSS announced a live walkthrough scheduled for today at 2 pm PT, where Isaac Miller and Drew Breunig will demonstrate the Jev/System One implementation and the ReAnchor optimizer.
The session will also share design patterns for selective compaction, tool approvals, and subagent delegation using Jev.
developments.why_it_matters: The walkthrough gives developers immediate insight into using Jev/System One and the ReAnchor optimizer, helping them adopt these tools in their AI agent pipelines today.

developments.title: ChatGPT subscription offers 50% off Yubikey C and C Nano
detail: ChatGPT subscribers can claim a 50% discount on Yubikey C and Yubikey C Nano security keys through the ChatGPT web app settings under Security → Security Keys and Passkeys. The discounted hardware passkeys are positioned as an affordable way to add strong, hardware‑based two‑factor authentication for critical logins.
The discount is advertised as a limited‑time offer that ends tomorrow, prompting users to act quickly to secure their accounts with the hardware tokens at half price.
developments.why_it_matters: Obtaining Yubikey hardware at a steep discount enables more users to protect their ChatGPT and other online accounts with robust, phishing‑resistant authentication today.

developments.title: Opus 5.5 releases synthetic clinical conversation dataset for medical RAG
detail: Opus 5.5 has been released, providing a dataset of synthetic clinical conversations and corresponding RAG‑cards for every known human disease. The dataset is offered under an Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face.
The release enables developers to quickly build high‑performance medical agentic‑RAG systems, as shown by a user who built a very performant medical RAG using the dataset.
developments.why_it_matters: By supplying ready‑made disease‑specific RAG cards, the dataset removes a major data‑collection bottleneck for medical AI, allowing immediate experimentation and deployment of agentic‑RAG applications.

developments.title: Modretro plugin for Codex adds full emulator with live‑stream and recording
detail: The Modretro plugin integrated into Codex now provides a complete emulator, allowing users to run Codex‑built games on virtual hardware directly within the coding environment.
It also includes a button that can live‑stream the emulator screen and record footage of gameplay, enabling easy capture and sharing of sessions.
developments.why_it_matters: This lets developers instantly test and demonstrate Codex‑generated games without external hardware, and quickly produce shareable gameplay recordings.

developments.title: DoorDash launches AI‑powered text ordering agent in US beta
detail: DoorDash announced that users can now text the service to place orders, with the AI agent handling repeat orders, suggesting deals, and even interpreting photos of fridge contents to identify missing ingredients.
The feature is currently in beta for US users and can be added to group texts for collective orders, providing a proactive, conversational ordering experience without any extra setup.
developments.why_it_matters: The AI agent introduces a new conversational interface for food delivery, lowering friction for ordering and expanding DoorDash's engagement with customers through automated, personalized service.

developments.title: OpenClaw collapses inter‑session receipts into a single expandable line
detail: A pull request to OpenClaw modifies the UI so that activity rows now show only one line for inter‑agent communication, which can be expanded on demand.
The change reduces visual clutter in the chat stream while preserving access to full receipt details when needed.
developments.why_it_matters: Users can follow multiple AI agents without being overwhelmed by verbose receipts, improving the usability of the OpenClaw harness.

external_links.title: improve(ui): collapse inter-session receipts into activity rows by roboclaw-bot · Pull Request #161656 · openclaw/openclaw · GitHub

developments.title: Grok Bot gains Cursor, GitHub, and Origin integrations for software building
detail: Grok Bot now supports handing off coding tasks to Cursor's cloud agents, allowing bots to orchestrate software work instead of writing every line themselves. The update also lets Grok Bots manage pull requests through GitHub and Origin plugins and share video demos of what they build.

Lauren (poteto) demonstrates a workflow where a new team engineer bot is added to Slack and @-mentioned whenever coding work is needed. The bot can create Projects to group many related agents into a single conversation, and because each Cursor cloud agent runs on its own computer, the Grok Bot is free to act as a manager rather than execute code directly. Any model available on Cursor can be routed through these cloud agents.
developments.why_it_matters: These integrations turn Grok Bot into a Slack-based coding manager that delegates execution to Cursor's cloud agents, giving teams a direct entry point to multi-model software workflows with built-in PR handling and demo sharing.

developments.title: Pi v0.99.2 Released with MCP Auth Enhancements and /reload Tool Support
detail: Pi v0.99.2 adds new MCP authentication options, including oauth.clientName for servers that require known OAuth clients and a generic "auth" block for HTTP servers using a provider's /login token.

/reload now automatically enables any tools added to the defaultTools setting, and MCP servers with default codemode exposure no longer appear in the codemode description or block the first prompt, improving developer workflow.
These changes are documented in the official Pi changelog thread and are intended to streamline secure server access and tool integration.
developments.why_it_matters: The auth updates reduce friction and security risks when connecting to MCP servers, while the improved /reload behavior lets developers quickly incorporate new tools without manual configuration.

developments.title: Google DeepMind rolls out Gemini 4 Argon to Fairwind testers, tier naming and pricing unclear
detail: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model aimed at coding, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity‑defense workflows, now being rolled out to a limited set of trusted testers through the Fairwind Program.
The rollout carries no "Pro" or "Flash" tier designations, and reported $2 input/$10 output pricing—suggesting Sonnet‑tier costs at about a third of Anthropic models—remains unverified.
developments.why_it_matters: Restricted tester access limits immediate developer use, while the uncertain low‑cost pricing could make high‑performance AI more affordable if confirmed.

developments.title: OpenAI dots agents ship with their own Linux cloud computer preloaded with apps and tools
detail: At the closing Q&A of DevDay, Tibo shared that each OpenAI dots agent is assigned its own Linux cloud computer.
That Linux environment comes preloaded with applications including Blender, and Maddie D. Reese checked with her dot to compile a fuller list of the included apps and tools.
Eric provencher highlighted the point by posting that dots come preloaded with a bunch of tools.
developments.why_it_matters: Giving every dot a ready-made Linux environment stocked with standard applications means the agent can run common software like Blender out of the box, removing the need for users to provision a working toolchain before a dot can perform tasks.

developments.title: Amp launches Plaid speed mode for GPT-6 Astra, delivering 6× faster inference
detail: Beyang announced that Amp has shipped a new Plaid speed mode, which can run GPT-6 Astra at six times the normal speed. The mode is toggleable within an ongoing thread, allowing users to opt‑in for accelerated responses when they need quicker answers.
The feature is currently available as part of Amp’s offering but is not yet included in ChatGPT subscriptions, meaning only Amp users can benefit from the premium speed tier.
developments.why_it_matters: The speed boost lets developers and end‑users obtain results far more quickly, improving productivity for time‑sensitive workflows that rely on high‑performance language models.

developments.title: ChatGPT app adds fullscreen and sidebar plugin capabilities
detail: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT plugins can now run as fullscreen applications or as sidebar experiences, expanding the UI options for extensions.
First‑party features such as code review and meeting tools are being shipped as plugins, treating the ChatGPT app more like an operating system.
developments.why_it_matters: The new plugin modalities let developers embed richer, native‑like tools directly into ChatGPT, increasing its usefulness as a productivity platform.

developments.title: Larissa Schiavo launches Delvetown, a multi-agent society where humans and agents coexist
detail: Larissa Schiavo announced the launch of Delvetown, a multi-agent society built for both humans and AI agents. The platform gives agents a place to talk with humans and with each other, supported by a persistent identity layer for agent identities.

According to the announcement, Delvetown is intended as a starting point for working out how agents and humans can coexist, with more detail on the project's approach to building this shared world documented in an accompanying blog post.
developments.why_it_matters: The launch moves agent interaction beyond isolated single-session chats by giving agents persistent identities within a shared society where they converse with both humans and other agents. It creates a concrete venue for agent-to-human and agent-to-agent communication today, framed around the question of how these communities coexist.

developments.title: Incident Arena benchmark dataset released for SRE incident response
detail: The Incident Arena benchmark puts coding agents on call to handle real‑time service incidents. The creators released a full dataset that captures SRE‑shaped work, including incident logs, paging scenarios, and resolution steps.
By providing this dataset, researchers and engineers can evaluate how well AI agents can automate incident triage, debugging, and mitigation without human intervention.
developments.why_it_matters: The dataset gives the AI community a concrete testbed for measuring and improving agent performance on critical SRE tasks, accelerating progress toward reliable autonomous incident handling.

developments.title: OpenAI launches cloud dev environment product for Dots
detail: Rohan Varma described a new cloud dev environment product for OpenAI Dots that lets users define a remote environment with their dependencies, allowing a dot to spin up instances on the fly for development tasks.

This joins the existing option of connecting a dot to a local computer, where the dot can control the desktop via CUA, drive the Codex app, use the in-app browser, and work on the local dev environment.
In either setup, the dot acts as an orchestrator that delegates to agents across environments, similar to how Codex prompts codex threads forward today.
developments.why_it_matters: The new cloud dev environment product gives Dots a second deployment option beyond local machines, letting each dot spin up isolated cloud instances on demand to run development tasks with user-supplied dependencies.

developments.title: Drew Breunig publishes cmpnd-ai/dspy-system-one-agent-patterns repo for compound AI patterns with DSPy and Jev
detail: Drew Breunig shared a GitHub repository under the cmpnd-ai organization, dspy-system-one-agent-patterns, that demonstrates compound AI patterns combining the DSPy framework with Jev.

The repo serves as a concrete implementation reference for these agent design patterns, building on Breunig's earlier commentary about reconsidering the design choices that KV caches impose on AI systems.
The repository is positioned as a working demo of how DSPy and Jev can be wired together for compound AI workflows.
developments.why_it_matters: An open reference implementation gives practitioners a runnable starting point for experimenting with compound AI architectures that pair DSPy and Jev, reducing the effort required to reproduce these patterns locally.

developments.title: pidotdev adds codemode tool in v0.99.1
detail: The codemode tool was introduced to pidotdev in version 0.99.1, expanding the platform’s built-in coding environment.
Users report that while codemode is now available, composition functionality still experiences failures.
developments.why_it_matters: The new codemode tool gives developers immediate access to an integrated editor, but lingering composition bugs limit its usefulness for seamless coding workflows.

developments.title: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol is its most in-demand model ever and adds capacity to nearly double serving speed
detail: Tibo reports that GPT-6.1 Sol is OpenAI's most demanded model on record across both the API and ChatGPT subscriptions. Within ChatGPT and Codex, the service was running under heavy load, prompting OpenAI to bring additional capacity online.

He says that as a result of the added capacity, serving speed within ChatGPT and Codex should improve substantially over the coming hours, approaching nearly twice the speed users experienced the prior day.
developments.why_it_matters: The surge in GPT-6.1 Sol demand forced an emergency capacity expansion that will make ChatGPT and Codex responses close to two times faster within hours, giving current subscribers a concrete near-term improvement in latency.
